intuition: Sorting every input value makes the kth largest easy to index, but it orders values that never affect the answer. We only need retain the strongest k candidates seen so far. A heap lets us maintain that group while reading the array once.

Use a min heap, even though the question asks for a largest rank. The root should be the weakest retained candidate, because that is the element to evict when a stronger value appears. Fill the heap until it has k values. Afterward ignore values no larger than its root and replace the root when a larger value arrives.

This preserves exactly the largest k processed values, including repeated values as separate items. The root of the final group is the kth largest: k-1 retained entries are at least as large, and every discarded entry is no larger. Distinct-value filtering would solve a different problem. For k=1 the heap keeps only the current maximum; for k equal to input length it keeps all values and exposes the minimum.

steps: For [3,2,1,5,6,4] with k=2, insert 3 and 2; the root is 2.
Read 1. It cannot improve the retained top two, so leave the heap unchanged.
Read 5 and replace root 2. The retained values are now 3 and 5.
Read 6 and replace root 3. The retained values become 5 and 6.
Read 4 and ignore it because it is below the current weakest retained value 5.
Return heap root 5, the second-largest value.

codeNotes.note: Before the retained group is full, every observed value must be admitted.
Only values stronger than the weakest retained candidate can improve the top-k group.
Replace the root in one bounded-heap operation while keeping the group size fixed.
